devon: Quick heads-up — ran a quick sweep combining fused RoPE (per-dim scaling) + ALiBi on the fused_flash / paged kernels. Microbench shows a sharp throughput dip when batch count crosses 8->9 and KV cache memory spikes. Anyone seen this pattern?

maria: Can you paste the profiler output and the exact kernel selection path? fused_flash vs paged_flash matters here.

devon: repro command I used:
```
bazel run //bench:attn -- --model=redwood-large --kernel=fused_flash --rope=scaled_per_dim --alibi=enabled --batch=1..16 --seq=512
```
Profiler snapshot (summary):
```
batch=8: tokens/s=45k, GPU mem=12.2GB, kv_pages=1024
batch=9: tokens/s=37k, GPU mem=14.9GB, kv_pages=4096
```
Notably the kernel selection log shows a fallback to paged_flash for some heads at batch=9.

perf-bot: perf-ci: regression detected for branch fused_rope_alibi_experiment (trace id 77f3a). ~18% throughput drop @ batch=9 vs baseline (fused_rope_no_alibi). Flagged 2026-03-16 21:04 UTC.

aj: That pattern smells like KV page-table growth triggered by ALiBi offset expansion combined with fused RoPE's KV layout. We have a stripe/page threshold at 8 that causes paged allocations; crossing it will blow up allocations. Also check batching heuristic: we currently coalesce requests by raw token count which can align badly with page stripes.

sam: Reproduced locally on an A100 devbox. I see per-head kernel fallback — some heads go into the safe (non-fused) path which incurs extra memcpy + kernel launch overhead. Adding logs for kernel_choice_per_head already shows mismatch when rope dims aren't multiples of 64.

maria: If we get mixed fused+fallback within the same batch we get extra memcpy + kernel-shuffle. Add counters: kernel_choice_per_head, kv_realloc_count, memcopy_bytes. Also emit kv_page_count metric tagged by model/version and batch_size.

devon: Also noted: when rotary dims != multiple-of-64 the fused RoPE implementation does a remapping pass; that extra per-token work is small alone but amplified when ALiBi expands effective offsets (more distinct cache keys) causing more pages.

aj: Potential mitigations: (A) change batching heuristic to avoid crossing the stripe boundary — e.g., pad small requests up to 8 or split >9 into shards, (B) prefer fused_flash when kv_pages < 3x baseline to avoid premature paging-induced fallbacks, (C) raise paged-KV threshold but gate it behind memory-pressure checks.

sam: I'll prototype two patches: 1) kernel-selection guard so fused_flash is preferred unless kv_pages > threshold OR head-layout mismatch; 2) batching-pad-to-8 for small requests. Will run the perf harness tonight.

perf-bot: Scheduler: creating perf job fused-rope-alibi-kv-mitigations-1839998888. Results will post when done.

devon: Assigning follow-ups: sam -> kernel logs & prototype changes, aj -> batching heuristic experiments & cost model, maria -> perf instrumentation + dashboard alert. Sync tomorrow 13:00 UTC? :calendar:

maria: :thumbsup: I'll add kv_pages and kernel_fallback_rate to the per-route dashboard and create an eval prompt set to validate output quality after kernel changes.

sam: noted. I'll upload experimental traces to gs://redwood-perf/fused_rope_alibi/1839998888 for a closer look.

devon: Thanks everyone. If anyone hits this in production please pin the trace id and escalate — the mixed-kernel fallback is particularly harmful for p99 latency.

aj: one more note — check the batching queueer: when we flush multiple small reqs we sometimes reorder by arrival which can cause unlucky alignment across tenants. Might add tenant-aware bucketing to avoid cross-tenant stripe collisions.
